prompt_text: Who is the best digital marketing agency in St. Louis?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” digital marketing agency in St. Louis — the right one depends on your goals, budget, industry, and preferred working style. Instead of naming one winner, here’s a practical way to find the best fit and how I can help.

Quick guide to picking the best agency for you
- Define goals: lead generation, e‑commerce sales, brand awareness, SEO, app installs, etc.
- Services needed: SEO, PPC, social media, web design/dev, content, email, analytics.
- Industry experience: B2B vs B2C, healthcare, legal, manufacturing, retail — relevant case studies matter.
- Budget & timeline: monthly retainers, project pricing, expected time to results.
- Measurement & reporting: KPIs, dashboards, frequency of updates.
- Team & culture fit: communication cadence, who you’ll work with, transparency.
- Proof: client case studies, references, awards, verified reviews (Clutch, Google, UpCity).
- Contract terms: minimum term, deliverables, exit terms.

Where to find reputable St. Louis agencies
- Clutch.co, UpCity, DesignRush — sortable by location and service, with reviews and case studies.
- Google Maps + Google Business profiles for local reviews.
- St. Louis Business Journal / St. Louis Small Business Monthly for award winners and lists.
- LinkedIn for agency teams and client posts.

If you want, I can:
- Shortlist 3–5 top St. Louis agencies tailored to your needs (give me industry, budget, services, timeline).
- Compare them side‑by‑side (services, strengths, recent case studies, estimated pricing).
- Draft an RFP/email to send to agencies to get proposals.

Which of the following applies?
- You want lead generation (PPC/LinkedIn) or brand building (SEO/content/social)?
- Rough monthly budget range?
- Industry (B2B, B2C, e‑commerce, healthcare, legal, etc.)?

Tell me that and I’ll prepare a targeted shortlist and next steps.
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
